title: Week Summary: Architecture as Stakeholder-Centered Design

concepts.name: Software architecture
concepts.description: The significant structures, decisions, principles, and rationale that shape a software-intensive system.

concepts.name: Architecturally significant decision
concepts.description: A design choice that has broad impact on qualities, cost, risk, interfaces, deployment, or future change.

concepts.name: Stakeholder concern
concepts.description: A need, risk, expectation, or constraint held by someone affected by the system or its architecture.

concepts.name: Architecture rationale
concepts.description: The reasoning that explains why an architectural decision was made and what alternatives were rejected.

concepts.name: Architecture description
concepts.description: A set of artifacts that records an architecture so stakeholders can understand, analyze, and use it.

concepts.name: Architecture view
concepts.description: A representation of a system from the perspective of one set of concerns.

concepts.name: Architecture model
concepts.description: A structured representation of architectural elements and relationships used for reasoning or communication.

concepts.name: Documentation fitness
concepts.description: The degree to which architecture documentation is useful, current, concise, and aligned with stakeholder needs.

concepts.name: Quality attribute
concepts.description: A measurable or discussable property of a system such as performance, security, usability, or modifiability.

concepts.name: Design constraint
concepts.description: A limitation or requirement that restricts the acceptable architecture choices.

concepts.name: Architecture tradeoff
concepts.description: A situation where improving one architectural concern can weaken or complicate another concern.

concepts.name: Architecture risk
concepts.description: An uncertainty or weakness in the architecture that may threaten a stakeholder concern.
